column3: NASB renders “the weak” as “those without strength” and adds “just.”
NASB follows the critical text without “for”; it adds “his.”
NASB follows the critical text; the quotation is in capitals. Stray spacing before the quotation appears in the NASB text.
NASB follows the critical text; “in the past” is rendered “in earlier times,” and “endurance” is “perseverance.”
NASB renders “of endurance” as “who gives perseverance” and “would give” as “grant.”
NASB renders “mouth” as “voice.”
NASB reads “us,” following other manuscripts; the critical text has “you.” “Receive” is rendered “accept.”
NASB follows the critical text (“For,” without “Jesus”); it adds “has.”
NASB adds “His”; the quotation is in capitals, and “praise” is rendered “GIVE PRAISE.”
The quotation is in capitals.
NASB follows the critical text (“let … praise”); the quotation is in capitals.
The quotation is in capitals; “There will be” is rendered “THERE SHALL COME.”
NASB renders “would fill” as “may … fill.”
NASB follows the critical text; “I have been persuaded” is rendered “I … am convinced.”
NASB follows the critical text without “brethren”; “more boldly” is rendered “very boldly,” and “in part” is “on some points.” It adds “again.”
NASB renders “administering the sacred service of” as “ministering as a priest” and adds “my.”
NASB follows the critical text; “I have the boasting” is rendered “I have found reason for boasting.”
NASB renders “dare” as “presume” and “unto” as “resulting in.”
NASB has “the Spirit” without “of God,” following manuscripts that lack it; “fully proclaimed” is rendered “fully preached.”
NASB renders “being ambitious” as “aspired” and adds “already.”
The quotation is in capitals. Stray spacing before the closing quotation mark appears in the NASB text.
NASB renders “many times” as “often.”
NASB renders “no longer having a place” as “with no further place for me” and restructures the verse.
NASB follows the critical text without “I will come to you”; it renders “to be equipped” as “to be helped on my way” and “I shall be filled” as “I have … enjoyed your company.”
Close to the Greek.
NASB renders “were pleased” as “have been pleased.”
NASB adds “Yes” and “to do so” and renders “debtors” as “indebted.”
NASB follows the critical text; “I will set off” is rendered “I will go on.”
NASB follows the critical text without “of the gospel.”
NASB renders “exhort” as “urge” and adds “your.”
